text:
Maria Lopez: Hey team — customer ran into an embeddings dimension mismatch after upgrading to ts-sdk 1.4.0. They see: "expected dim 1536 but got 768" when calling /embeddings.
Alex Chen: Oof. Is this the model switch issue (large vs small)? Any logs or request payload?
Maria Lopez: They sent a batch of 4 texts, using the batcher in ts-sdk. Attached log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T18:12:02Z INFO batches: sending batch id=bb-22 size=4 model=text-embedding-3-small
2026-03-15T18:12:02Z DEBUG req: embedding.request_id=01F... payload_dim=1536
2026-03-15T18:12:03Z ERROR response: embedding.dim_mismatch expected=1536 got=768
```
Alex Chen: Hmm payload_dim shows 1536 but server returns 768. Could the batcher be multiplexing requests for different model variants into one request?
Maria Lopez: Customer claims they set model per-call to text-embedding-3-large (1536) but our batcher config uses defaultModel=text-embedding-3-small for throughput. Looks like a misbatch where calls for large got merged with small.
Kevin Patel: @Alex can you check the ts-sdk batch key logic? I remember a recent optimization that groups by route+modelKey but might have used model alias rather than resolved canonical model id.
Alex Chen: Repro steps from customer:
1) Install @redwood/ts-sdk v1.4.0
2) call client.embeddings.batch([...], { model: 'text-embedding-3-large' }) concurrently with other calls that omit model (rely on default)
3) occasional failures with dim mismatch or truncated vectors
Code they used:
```
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await Promise.all(texts.map(t => client.embeddings.create({ model: 'text-embedding-3-large', input: t })));
```
Julia Park: Could also be a race in resolving defaultModel from config when batcher captures the group key. If alias resolution async and returns small for some, batching will mix.
Maria Lopez: Customer says error rate ~3% at 250qps. They set retries to 2 and backoff exponential but still see some broken responses.
Kevin Patel: I'm going to reproduce locally. Quick check: @support-bot can you attach customer's request id (they provided rw-req-id=rw_5Xb...) logs?
support-bot: Attached logs for rw_5Xb... (s3://redwood-support/attachments/rw_5Xb_logs.gz) :paperclip:
Alex Chen: Found a code path in batcher where batchKey = `${route}:${modelAlias||default}` but modelAlias may be undefined and default is resolved after batch started. Patch idea: include resolvedModelId in the key and make the model resolution sync before enqueuing.
Kevin Patel: Also noticed backoff config in ts-sdk uses fixed delay for retries in 1.4.0 which can cause thundering retries that amplify misbatches. Need jittered exponential backoff.
Maria Lopez: Customer asked if they should workaround by pinning defaultModel to large on client init. Is that safe?
Alex Chen: Yes as short-term workaround: instantiate with defaultModel: 'text-embedding-3-large' and set batchWindowMs smaller (e.g., 10ms) to reduce mixing.
Kevin Patel: I've opened internal issue ENG-ML-998 and a PR in ts-sdk repo with two fixes: 1) resolve model id synchronously when enqueuing, 2) change retry backoff to jittered exp. Reference PR #412.
Maria Lopez: Thanks — I told customer we'll provide a patched package or they can apply the workaround. Can we get an ETA?
Kevin Patel: Patch ready, running unit+integration tests against embedding service. If green, publish v1.4.1 tomorrow morning PST.
Maria Lopez: Marking as P1 for the customer. I created a support ticket SUP-2026-719 and linked logs.
Julia Park: After patch we should add an e2e test that simulates mixed-model concurrent calls to ensure no cross-batching. Also add metric for batch model-id variance.
Alex Chen: Agreed. I'll add tests and the metric.
Maria Lopez: Customer response: "Thanks, will try the workaround and wait for v1.4.1. Appreciate the quick help :rocket:"
deploy-bot: Release v1.4.1 candidate built (sha: d4f7a9) - running canary deploy to staging :construction:
Kevin Patel: Following up tomorrow with the release notes and guidance to set retries/backoff. Closing loop once customer confirms recovery. :white_check_mark:
